transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?
I’m here because I keep snapping at people. At a safety meeting, I started yelling before I could stop myself, and now the younger inspectors seem scared to even ask me anything.
Would you say this kind of quick-temper reaction is something new that started recently, or has it been a pattern for you going back many years?
It’s been happening recently. I keep snapping at people before I can stop myself—like at that safety meeting, I started yelling, and now the younger inspectors seem afraid to come ask me things.
Did something particularly stressful or upsetting happen around the time this irritability started?
Yes. It started after that machinery accident, not long after we switched to the overnight schedule. That was about two years and four months ago.
Since the accident, have you had any unwanted, intrusive memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about it that keep coming back to you?
Yes. A clank from a cart, or the smell of hot oil, can put me right back in that bay. I see my coworker by the machine like it’s happening right in front of me again.
During that machinery accident, did you hit your head, lose consciousness, or sustain any physical injury?
I’m not sure. Everything happened so fast, and I don’t really remember whether I hit my head or blacked out.

Since the accident, have you noticed any new problems with your memory, concentration, or ability to think clearly—things like forgetting tasks you used to handle easily or losing your train of thought?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed anything specific like that, at least not that I can point to.
Since the accident, have you found yourself avoiding certain places, tasks, or people that remind you of what happened?

Yes. I go out of my way not to pass the inspection bay. And I don’t like talking about the accident if I can avoid it. I used to go to these industrial-history talks, but I stopped—the pictures of the old machinery just set me off.
Since the accident, have you noticed yourself feeling constantly on edge, easily startled by sudden noises, or unusually watchful of your surroundings, even in safe settings?

Yes. Even in the break room, or at rehearsal, I keep watching the doors and listening for sudden machine noises. I’m always checking who’s moving behind me. It’s like my body just won’t believe I’m safe.
